Dated this the 8th day of August, 2025  ORDER
This bail application is filed under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS').

2. Petitioner is the accused in Crime No.1739/2025 of Thiruvalla Police Station, Pathanamthitta;
registered for the offences punishable under Sections 354D(1)(i), 354D(1)(ii), 366, and 376(2)(n) of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Section 64(2)(m) and 69 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.
3. The prosecution case is that, the defacto complainant, unmarried lady, became acquainted with the accused in 2022 who had projected himself as divorcee and ready to marry her.

Thereafter the parties engaged in a physical relationship with the defacto complainant on several occasions under a promise to marry, and later the accused failed to marry her and thus committed the offences alleged.
Petitioner was arrested on 02.07.2025 and he has been in custody since then.
4 . Heard Sri.Sunil Kumar M., the learned counsel for the petitioner, as well as Smt.Sreeja V., the learned Public Prosecutor.
5. Defacto complainant specifically alleged that after becoming acquainted BAIL APPL. NO. 9090 OF 2025 2025:KER:59450 with the accused, he came to her house with a proposal to marry her.
Later, he confessed that he was married and was about to obtain a divorce, stating that upon a payment of Rs.7,00,000/- as compensation to his wife, the divorce will be finalised.
The defacto complainant allegedly pledged her gold ornaments and handed over Rs.7,00,000/- to him.
Thereafter, she repeatedly requested him to show her the divorce papers.

However, he delayed Byju.T.R vs State Of Kerala on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120808237/
2 showing her the same, but asserted that he was already divorced, and thereafter, he indulged in a physical relationship with the defacto complainant at various places including PWD rest houses in various districts and other lodges.
The defacto complainant also states that the accused had introduced her as his wife at the Collectorate in Idukki.
However, petitioner has not fulfilled his promise and continues to remain married.

6. The above circumstances, as evidenced from the statement of the defacto complainant, indicate that the accused had induced her to engage in a physical relationship after projecting him to be a divorcee.
The circumstances would reveal a situation where the petitioner, under the guise of a promise to marry compelled the defacto complainant to engage in a physical relationship.
Since the allegations are serious and the investigation is still not complete, I am of the view that releasing the petitioner on bail at this stage would prejudice the investigation.
Hence, this bail application is dismissed.
